articleTitle: Smart farm prototype for plant disease detection, diagnosis & treatment using IoT device in a greenhouse
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: One common problems faced by farmers is to identify the diseases in plants. Just relying on naked eyes to detect diseases is very difficult. We propose the development of a cost-effective and affordable smart farming prototype that can detect plant diseases in advance and notify farmers so that remedial actions could be taken. Also, a web-based system has been developed to allow the farmers to monitor the status of their plants in the greenhouse. The development of such a smart farming plant disease detection system will allow farmers to have the ability to detect diseases at an early stage of the plants which will minimize yield loss from full-blown disease outbreak in their greenhouse. One important feature of this system is its ability to categorise the Septoria plant disease for which categorizing the stages of the disease outbreak on the leaf is very important. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that machine learning classification algorithm can be used in raspberry pi without losing performance. Based on our tests we also find that random forest classifier with colour histogram is the best combination to be run by this prototype for efficient plant disease detection.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of single-axis and dual-axis solar tracking systems
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Solar panel facing the sun generates the highest power available. This paper provides a method on how a single-axis and dual-axis solar tracking method can be performed through a technique by tracking the sun according to the sun's irradiation. Two LDR sensors and a motor is used for single-axis tracking system and 4 LDR sensors and 2 motors for dual-axis tracking system. Voltage and current readings from the solar panel rated 7.5 V have been rescaled usingvoltage divider circuit. The readings are then calculated by the microcontroller and have been displayed to a Display (GLCD). All simulation experiments have been tested using commercially-available Proteus simulation software. Measurement of voltage, current, and power calculated and recorded by the microcontroller are accurate with about 1.4% error. The system operations were successful whereby the software programming when connected to an actual circuit will be able to track the sun by the sun's light intensity.

articleTitle: Assessing small group assignments
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The practice of group assignments in Higher Education Institutions is argued to save time to teaching staffs and allow students to develop a range of skill-sets. However, assessing group works and consequent allocation of marks to individual students in a group is challenging. This paper presents an overview of available techniques for mark allocation to individual group members, presents an effort-based mark allocation scheme, and summarises the observations from implementing the scheme. It was observed that students have mixed opinion on differential treatment of individual marks on the basis of their contribution to delivering the group assignment. However, students were found to be appreciative of the scheme when they were engaged in the decision making process of how to assess their works and consequent apportionment of marks to individual members of the group.

articleTitle: Fast pyrolysis system of biomass solid waste for bio-oil
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Biomass solid waste in the form of rice husk obtained from Brunei's high yielding Laila paddy rice was collected locally, processed, dried and fast pyrolyzed in a fixed bed stainless steel pyrolysis reactor of 5 cm diameter and 51 cm length. The rice husk was grounded to a particle size of 0.6–0.85 mm and oven dried until 9% of moisture was removed. The fast pyrolysis system was designed, fabricated and tested. Mixture of sawdust and gas was used as heating source with the weight proportion of 10:1. The fast pyrolysis system was run for 1 hour at temperatures ranging from 350°C to 550°C with an apparent vapor residence time of 5 seconds. A maximum bio-oil yield of 36% by wt. of dry biomass feedstock was obtained at an optimum temperature of 450°C with 41% biochar yield. The variation of product yields was presented with pyrolysis reactor bed temperature and particle size. The higher heating value of the bio-oil was determined by an oxygen bomb calorimeter to be 21.75 MJ/kg, with a density of 1,007 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and an acidic pH value of 3.32. The solid char higher heating value was found to be 28.4 MJ/kg with a density of 356 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Prediction of rain rate distribution with time delay based on measured 1-min rain intensity data to mitigate fades on satellite link
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Earth to satellite communications are moving towards higher frequency bands in future which are more sensitive to environment. Rain causes severe degradation in performances at higher frequency bands specially in tropical regions. Several mitigation techniques are proposed by researcher to design reliable system. Time diversity is one of the potential candidate for it. However, time diversity analysis requires measured rain attenuation data. For future high frequency link design those data are not available at most of the places. This paper proposes a method to utilize 1-min rain rate to analyse time diversity technique at any desired frequency. In proposed method, it is assumed that rain rate with delay can represent rain attenuation with delay for same period of time at same location. This assumption is valid as long as the attenuation causes due to rain. A model is developed to predict rain rate distribution with delay from annual measured statistics.

articleTitle: The role of strategic management & project management to organisational success
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Organisations operate in dynamic environment and strive to survive and succeed in long run through structured act of management. This is usually approached through strategic management, focusing on continuous improvements in operational arrangements. However, the priority is on project management for organisational success in construction industry. It is therefore important to examine if, and how, strategic management is practiced in construction industry. Overall methodology of this research includes literature review, questionnaire survey and interviews. However, this paper is based on initial but structured review of literature to examine the commonalities and/or differences between the two management approaches and their contributions to organisational success. This paper then proposes a conceptual framework which combines both approaches based on their commonalities, to achieve organisational success. It is suggested that the collaboration between the two management approaches is critical for organisations to accomplish success.

articleTitle: Q-switched erbium doped fiber laser using copper nanoparticles polyvinyl alcohol as saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The generation of passively Q-switched Erbium-doped fiber laser (EDFL) by using copper nanoparticles polyvinyl alcohol as a passive saturable absorber (SA) was experimentally demonstrated. The copper nanoparticles powder is dissolved in tetrahydrofuran (THF). Then, the end solution was added and mixed thoroughly with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) suspension to form a thin film based SA and sandwiched between two ferrules in an EDFL cavity. A Q-switched operation was obtained within the pump power range of 8.93mW to 97.6mW. The pulse repetition rate showed an increasing trend from 19.89kHz to 84.0kHz, whereas the pulse width exhibited a decreasing trend from 22.96μ5 to 4.6μ5. The highest pulse energy of 95.8nJ was obtained at pump power of 97.6mW. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 62dB obtained indicates the stability of the Q-switched pulse generated.

articleTitle: An overview of construction related pollution
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Construction industry considerably contributes to the economy of a country; however, it is also a major polluter. Numerous researches have been done regarding pollution from construction activities, which are broadly classified as air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution, and solid waste. However, those are often country specific and their degree and nature may vary according to the type of construction project as well, e.g. low-rise building, high-rise building, and infrastructure projects. Moreover, it appears to have no research conducted before regarding pollution from construction in Brunei Darussalam. The present research intends to fill this gap; as such this paper summarizes the sources of different kinds of pollution originating from construction activities and their potential mitigating strategies.

articleTitle: Utilization of microtremor measurements to evaluate fundamental frequency in Urban settlement of Taxila-Pakistan
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The present study has been conducted on Taxila, Pakistan to understand its local geology and its suspected contribution to disaster during a seismic event. The Nakamura technique was applied to estimate fundamental frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, spectral ratio amplitude A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, and alluvium thickness H along 16 selected sites in the study area. The estimated values for fundamental frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> lie between 0.7 and 11.3 Hz, spectral ratio amplitude A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ranges between 1.02 and 3.9 and the alluvium thickness H ranges between 2.91 and 216.79 meters. ARC GIS maps were also designed to show the spatial extent of the site response parameters. The results were then correlated with borehole data to enhance the credibility of the result. The results inferred through the study indicated that the study area exhibits an overall low fundamental frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> thus reflecting greater alluvium thickness H and consequently high susceptibility to damage amplification by local site effects.

articleTitle: Effect of product service system-inventory control integration on the industrial perspective in manufacturing industry
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Global competitive and effective product development cycles increase pressure on manufacturing companies. Product Service System (PSS) research empirically examines sustainability of company performance and growth. As a result, implementing PSS from a manufacturing perspective requires diverse approaches and techniques to be adopted. Inventory Control in PSS creates a larger set of uncertainties that the factory needs to manage, due to the enhanced scope and complexity of the product and service offering. The aim of the research is to create a strategic approach to identify, analyse, and optimise the inventory control of PSS. An important motivation of this research relates to its ambition to combine the two areas: PSS and inventory control which have not traditionally come together. Research will be done in four stages (i.e literature study, study a system at Company A, develop a generic model, design architecture of PSS Inventory Control). This work will contribute to the current PSS research by developing a generic model of PSS Inventory Control of PSS Inventory Control from manufacturing operations perspectives and PSS Inventory financial model.

articleTitle: CO2 activated carbon from oil palm shell using microwave temperature as process parameter
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The utilization of microwave technology to prepare activated carbons have been intensified with the improvement in the microwave technology. However, research into the use of temperature as a control parameter in microwave heating is still in the early stage. This study has been able to successfully used bed temperature as a process parameter during both carbonization and activation process. The carbonization and activation were conducted in a domestic microwave that was modified to accommodate the quartz reactor and incorporated with PID temperature controller. The introduction of temperature controller allowed for effective and efficient determination of the heating rate, carbonization and activation temperature. The results obtained show that temperature as well as irradiation time hugely impacted on the porosity development of the activated carbon with little or no impact on the yield of the activated carbon. Preparation at optimal conditions of bed temperature 900 °C and irradiation time of 40 min yielded activated carbon with a BET surface area 571.37 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, total pore volume 0.244 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and micropore volume of 0.198 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> g"<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.

articleTitle: Experimental design and optimization of flat plate collector using Taguchi method
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Factors affecting the collector efficiency of a laboratory scale solar thermal system were identified and further investigated. This paper used Taguchi method to investigate the optimum level of each of the factors (control parameters) identified. Twenty-seven number of experiments were conducted. The result from signal-to-noise ratio analysis shows that by using ethylene glycol solution as the heat transfer fluid, selective heat absorber plate as the heat absorber plate, receiving highest solar intensity, no preheating of water bath, highest possible volumetric flowrate and lowest fraction of cloud cover, the performance of the flat plate collector could be optimized. The ANOVA performed found that the utilization of different heat exchange plate, heat transfer fluid and the covering the flat plate collector (cloud cover) contributed the highest change in collector efficiency with the 48.1%, 30% and 15.4%, respectively. The contributions of other parameters produced insignificant effect. The parameters considered here can be a preliminary experimental investigation towards optimizing the efficiency of a small laboratory scale flat plate collector.

articleTitle: Statistical correlation between road surface roughness and traffic accidents
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Road surface condition is widely accepted as one of the most important factors that affect the safety of a land transport system. Although various researchers examined different types of surface condition, only a few focused on how road roughness, particularly quantified by International Roughness Index (IRI), can contribute to the occurrences of Road Traffic Accidents (RTA). Previous studies have found no consistent correlation and trend between both variables due to different regression techniques adopted, and the inclusion and exclusion of different contributory factors. This paper presents an analysis of the influence of IRI and various types of road properties on the observed number of accidents (μ-value) using a statistical regression analysis. The study road, where the accident and road properties were examined, was a high-traffic volume and high-speed highway section in Brunei Darussalam. The outcome of the analysis has indicated that the IRI values have a weak correlation to the observed number of accidents given that other explanatory variables are included into the regression. Limitations of the statistical regression acquired are discussed and recommendations to refine the selected variables and analysis methods are provided.

articleTitle: Etched fiber Bragg grating sensor for lead ion detection
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to detect the concentrations of Lead ion (Pb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>) in Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) solution using an etched Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensor. The sensor was etched using 48% hydrofluoric (HF) acid solution to function as a chemical sensor. When the proposed sensor is exposed to various concentrations of Pb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> solutions, the Bragg wavelength (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>) shifts due to change in the effective refractive index (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>), affected by the change of refractive index of the solution. The sensitivity achieved by this sensor is 5.0 × 10-3nm/ppm and the overall shifting of the Bragg wavelength is 0.027nm from 0–50 ppm.

articleTitle: Investigation of liquid flow interaction on wax and cut channel paper-based microfluidic analytical device (μPAD)
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Simple, user-friendly, economical and rapid sensing devices are in urgent demand for diagnostics purposes especially in resource-limited countries. Diagnostics devices fabricated from patterning paper into hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions called paper-based microfluidic analytical devices (μPADs) have been introduced. In this work, straight line handcrafted channel at dimension of 3 mm width have been constructed as an inexpensive method of fabrication for wax and cut μPADs channel. For wax channel, wax hydrophobic channel is drawn on the upper side of the paper and heated for 3 minutes on 100 °C of hotplate for the diffusion of wax into the thickness of paper. 10 different viscosities of sucrose solution ranging from 0% to 70% of solute with additional of 2 blind samples is pipetted into the wax and cut channel and left horizontally for liquid flow in a minute. The flow rate is calculated. 3 types of paper which are filter paper, chromatography paper and litmus paper have been tested. In summary, it can be concluded that more viscous liquid will slow down the flow rate of liquid travel inside the wax channel compared to the cut channel and filter paper is chosen as the materials for the fabrication of μPADs channel.

articleTitle: Design and modeling of a smart insole hybrid energy harvester
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Miniaturization of wearable electronics attracted researchers towards technologically harvesting tiny wattages of power for sustainability and supplementation of batteries. This can guarantee increased leisure in achieving autonomous wireless sensing and measurement applications in far-off locations. Human body mechanics and vibrations presents a viable way of harvesting energy to overcome the limitation of non-stop power supply to wearable electronics which is in fact a constraint for lasting operation of these implantable devices in embedded and remote locations. This paper reports bio-mechanical hybrid energy harvesting from heel strike. The prototype exhibit multi resonant frequencies in the range of 1Hz, 3Hz and 10Hz. The harvester can produce power in milliwatts (mW) which is sufficient to operate a monitoring sensor or a wireless sensor node (WSN).

articleTitle: Vent system design for bulk road tankers filling stations involved in loading volatile refinery products
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The road tanker filling stations are provided near the bulk storage facilities to load the petroleum products to road tankers. While filling the Road Tankers, the hydrocarbons and air mixture will be vented from the tankers to atmosphere through vent stack. This paper describes the methodologies of the vent stack design and selection criterions for the stack location. It also recommends the basis for performing hydraulics for the vent header and stack.

articleTitle: Slow pyrolysis system of agricultural solid waste for bio-char
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Agricultural solid waste of sugarcane bagasse was pyrolyzed in a fixed bed stainless steel pyrolysis reactor of 7.6 cm diameter and 90 cm length. The bagasse is prepared into 2–4 mm size range and oven-dried to remove moisture. The slow pyrolysis system was run at temperatures ranging from 250 "C to 400"C with an apparent vapour residence time of 50 seconds and nitrogen gas flow rate of 5 litre/mins. A maximum bio-char yield of 45.9% by wt of dry biomass feedstock was obtained at temperature of 250°C. The highest liquid yield was 26.3% by wt of dry biomass feedstock obtained at 400"C. The rest was gas that had been flared to atmosphere. The running time for the experimental run was 1 hour. The variation of product yields is presented with pyrolysis reactor bed temperature. The bio-char and bio-oil were characterized for its properties. The higher heating value of the bio-char yield was determined by an oxygen bomb calorimeter and this was found to be 30.6 MJ/kg. The density of the bio-char was found to be 228 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Thus, the energy density of the bio-char was estimated to be 6.97 GJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The higher heating value for the bio-oil was 17.8 MJ/kg.

articleTitle: A Simulink block for quadrotor rotorcraft motion animation
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Flight profile is essential in describing the motion of a flying vehicle. In control systems simulation, data can simply be visualized in a time-based graph. Complement to this, visualization through animation could promote better understanding in the case of multi-degree motion e.g. six degrees of freedom (6DOF). Hence, this paper describes the implementation of a custom block to animate the motion of a quadrotor rotorcraft in the MathWorks® Simulink® environment. The block can animate quadrotor rotorcraft motion data from 1DOF up until 6DOF and equipped with several configurable features. The block may be used as a supplementing tool in the control systems study related to quadrotor rotorcraft as it allows researcher to visualize the rotorcraft motions through an animation.

articleTitle: Investigation of energy uses in oil and gas industry in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Energy efficiency in oil and gas industry is of a paramount importance and the economy of Brunei Darussalam is mainly based on this industry. Aim of the paper is to present Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) in production and utility of the industry. In addition, energy efficiency in production is presented. The energy consumption and production data related to crude oil production is obtained from the Brunei Shell Petroleum company (BSP), and for the natural gas plant is provided by the Brunei Liquefied Natural Gas company (BLNG). The energy consumption in BSP and BLNG is categorized into production and utility. The production category is subdivided into three: gas compression, condensate stabilizer and reformer. The consumption of energy in utility is in storage and transportation of oil and gas. Investigation is based on data from year 2011 to 2015 in the current study. It is found that the average SEC in production at BSP is 202 kWh/bbl. It is found that the energy consumption for production is between 168–315 kWh/bbl [1]. The utility SEC at BSP is found to be 14.85 kWh/bbl. The SEC in utility is 7% of the SEC in production. The efficiency of production in BSP is found to be 88%. The average SEC in production at BLNG is found to be 772 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of Liquefied Natural gas (LNG) equivalent to 1.28 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of Natural Gas. The efficiency of production at BLNG is found to be 88%. The efficiency in production at United States refinery is within a range of 84–88% [2], Hence, the efficiency in production at BSP and BLNG is comparable with the US refinery. It is thus concluded that the oil and gas industry in Brunei Darussalam is operating within an acceptable range of SEC and efficiency. In future, the research could be extended to other industries in Brunei Darussalam.

articleTitle: Investigation of the characteristics of PV system for different irradiances and temperatures
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Renewable energy system is of highly significant focus at this time. Establishment of this system is desirable due to the limitation of conventional power system. Photovoltaic (PV) system is one method in which it can produce renewable energy in the form of power system. In PV system, irradiance and temperature are the key factors in order to determine the condition of the output. In this paper, different values of irradiance and temperature have been considered to monitor the PV module characteristics of a single array and full array of PV for single-phase and there-phase systems.

articleTitle: Energy efficient approaches in passive optical network: A review
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: A passive optical network (PON) has provided a better solution in network communication due to its capability of delivering a high volume of bandwidth and speed. However, it is known that most of the energy consumption in the communications network is from PONs within the access network. Thus, researchers from either academia and industry have continually worked to find an energy-efficient solution to minimize the energy consumption. In this paper, the most relevant research works to reduce energy consumption in telecom networks, especially at the access network level, employing the optical technologies presented.

articleTitle: Power system analysis using SKM power tools
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The size and complexity of modern power systems impose significant challenges in the power system analysis, control and management of the system. SKM Power Tools software [1] is used to accurately simulate real events that occur in an electrical power network to easily understand the dynamics of any changes made to the network. This paper will be examining the use of the SKM Power Tools software, by SKM Systems Analysis Inc., to perform a power system analysis in a project involving upgrade of an existing power distribution system.

articleTitle: Identifying sub-groups of the obese from national health and nutritional status survey data using machine learning techniques
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The aim of this study is to discover unknown but meaningful patters (groups) from the National Health and Nutritional Status and Survey (NHANSS) data by applying clustering analysis technique. This study focuses on determining the association of obesity, one of the leading causes of common non-communicable diseases, with the identified clusters. The subsets within NHANSS data were identified for obesity using various parameters including socio-demographic factors, physical activity and multiple dietary patterns of the participants

articleTitle: An exact method for computing the delay margin for the LFC system in Microgrid
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The Microgrid central controller monitors the frequency to guarantee stable operation. The control signals are exchanged through communication network where the time delay is inevitable. Not considering the time delay could lead to system instability and hence the delay margin for the system stability should be calculated. In this paper, we propose a new method for computing the delay margin of the load frequency control system in the Microgrid. The load frequency control system is modelled as a time delay system. The transcendental time delay characteristics equation is transformed to frequency depending equation. The spectral radius is used to find the frequencies at which the roots cross the imaginary axis. The values of the crossing frequencies are determined through the sweeping test and the binary iteration algorithm. A Microgrid consists of diesel generator and PV source is used as case study. The proposed method determines the delay margin exactly which is verified through time domain simulation.

articleTitle: ANFIS approach for locating faults using GPS coordinates in a distribution system
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Power utilities are increasingly concerned about the issues on quality and reliability of power supply system to accomplish low Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI). One of the important aspects to assure high quality and reliability of power supply is to handle faults in distribution networks. Faults need to be located accurately and as quickly as possible before appropriate action can be taken. This paper presents the development of an intelligent technique to locate faults in a power distribution system. The proposed technique implements the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) for fault location in latitate and longitute as GPS coordinates. The output of the proposed method provides information such as type of fault and fault address from google map by using the post-fault three-phase current data. The results of ANFIS training show that the average error is almost zero for each types of fault, 0.004 for latitate coordinate and also almost zero for longitute coordinate. Simulations were carried out by using the commercial software package PSS-ADEPT to validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A brief overview of greening existing buildings
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Implementing the concept of green building is suitable in new buildings, but there exist a huge number of old buildings, which are crafted with modern, sustainable and energy efficient features to improve energy efficiency and environmental performance of old buildings. Thus, greening existing buildings significantly reduces energy consumption, and improves environmental and other performance levels. Overall methodology used for this research includes literature review, questionnaire survey and interviews. However, this paper summarises the outcomes from the structured literature review only. A total of 19 commonly used green features were identified. It is observed that those green features target improvement of efficiency in four different areas, namely energy efficiency, water efficiency, indoor air quality and materials use. This will form the basis for further study of exploring the degree of benefits of certain green features and its consequent selection / used in specific building types.

articleTitle: Investigation of wasteful activities to improve construction productivity: In perspective of construction in Astana, Kazakhstan
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Construction industry is highly characterized by its low productivity due to the presence of wasteful activities in many forms. The key idea of lean principles is to maximize process value while minimizing waste. This study aims to explore and quantify the impact on construction productivity by non-value adding items. Several observations were made for construction operations in Astana, Kazakhstan to quantify various types of wasteful activities. It was observed that 26% activities were pure waste. Nevertheless, the literature study provided the percentage of non-value adding activities to be between 36–65%. Moreover, other sources of waste such as "Preparation" and "Break" were found from the observations which do not fall under any of the existing 7 waste categories. A questionnaire survey was also conducted to examine the general understanding of non-value adding activities in construction. Most of the survey participants also indicated the presence of wasteful activities in the construction processes to be between 10–30%. Finally, to improve the construction productivity by properly quantifying the non-value adding activities, Value Stream Mapping (VSM) tool which is also evidenced by the survey result, was found to be most effective lean tool since it facilitates increased visualization.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic simulation of a selected reach in a tidal river
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: A 2D hydrodynamic and time dependent model was applied to a 30 km selected portion in an ungauged semi-diurnal tidal river connected to the Bay of Bengal. A model setup was done for this data scarce reach based on mostly primary data using Delft3D model. Simulation was carried out for continuous 216 hours. Hydraulic characteristics were determined for the transient conditions i.e. water levels vary with time. The reported model showed reasonable outcome (i.e., R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>= 0.84) compare to the observed data. The hydrodynamic simulation is the prime requirement for conducting further tidal simulation as well as salinity intrusions both in the estuary and studied river, those will be covered in the next phase of this study. Therefore, this study envisaged to provide guidance to the Decision Support System.

articleTitle: Towards a sustainable consumption of water for households in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Households are the largest water users in Brunei Darussalam. This is in contrast with other countries where agriculture accounts for most water consumption followed by industry and domestic uses. Water tariffs in Brunei are subsidised and these low tariffs lead to high water consumption. The high usage has raised awareness of the importance of water conservation in Brunei. This paper investigates the pattern of water consumption among Bruneian households. The paper also attempts to find ways to reduce household water consumption. One way to reduce household water consumption would be to increase the water tariffs. However, this paper suggests that raising water prices may not be appropriate for Brunei, because water price has remained low for the last 40 years and people are used to it. As an alternative to price increase, this paper suggests that change of consumption slab may be helpful to reduce domestic water consumption. The water authority of Brunei may bring down the upper limit to 45 cubic metres from its current value of 54.54 cubic metres of water consumption per month.

articleTitle: 3D seismic interpretation and structural modelling of bend conglomerate of Atoka group, Boonsville field Texas USA
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The objectives of this study are to provide geological visualizations of the targeted formations of the Boonsville field, stratigraphic interpretation to identify different geological features in the interpreted formations and to identify the hydrocarbon prospects within the study formations. In addition, stratigraphic interpretations and 3D models in time and depth domains were also analyzed to better visualize geological and stratigraphic settings in the subsurface of the area of interest.

articleTitle: Sand erosion prediction in a centrifugal pump
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: In the present study, 3D simulations of a centrifugal pump are presented using Vista CPD with the aid of ANSYS software. The CFD analysis of centrifugal pump used steady Reynold-averaged Navier-Stokes equating along with the k — ε turbulence model. The pump performance is presented as the fluid head against capacity of the pump for different rotational speed. Detailed contours plot of pressure and velocity vectors are shown for different operating conditions. Simulation for the sand erosion rate at different rotational speed and different particle size were also carried out. Results showed that head is a function of capacity and the erosion rate increases with increasing either the speed or particle size.

articleTitle: Characterization of rice husk as a potential renewable energy source
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Four different varieties of rice husk from Bangladesh were the studied biomass as the potential renewable energy resource in biomass gasification integrated solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) based combined heat and power generation (CHP). The heating value, moisture content, pellet density, bulk density, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) were carried out. The heat of combustion determined by using bomb calorimeter showed that the high heating values (HHVs) of rice husk are in the range 12–19 MJ/kg. Moisture content analysis revealed in the range 5–8 wt. %. The bulk densities of rice husk were proved to be suitable for storage and transportation. SEM showed the microstructure images of rice husk and rice husk ash. EDX detected remarkable levels of O and C in the examined rice husks and the extra peak of Si in rice husk ash. The use of rice husk ash as by product was presented.

articleTitle: A review of transport demand modelling for the school run in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Brunei Darussalam is one of the most car-dependent countries in the world. The low cost of running a car, driven by a Government policy of subsidising fuel, continues to ensure the car is the preferred option for almost all trips including school run. This high car dependency leads to heavy traffic congestion outside schools and this is exacerbated as Brunei has an atypical school traffic pattern due to its unique education systems. This causes many urban roads in Brunei to have a unique traffic flow profile, with a very prominent midday peak. Transportation planning is essential in order to improve and increase the efficiency of the country's transportation system. This study thus attempts to present an overview of state of art of various methods of travel demand modelling, in order to find the most suitable method for modelling the school run situation and enable potential solutions to be proposed and evaluated. It is found that research is still required in order to develop travel demand models for school run and also to find other solutions to solve the issue of school-related congestion.

articleTitle: High nonlinear coefficients of photonic crystal fiber with ultra-flattened chromatic dispersion
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a unique highly nonlinear dispersion-flattened photonic crystal fiber (HNDF-PCF) via numerical simulation using the full vector finite difference method (FDM). Simulation results show that it is possible to get high nonlinear coefficient larger than 51W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> at 1.55μm wavelength, near zero ultra-flattened chromatic dispersion of 0 ± 0.4ps/(nm.km) which covers E+S+C+L telecommunication band, low chromatic dispersion slope of − 0.003ps/(nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.km) and very low confinement losses of less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup>dB/km in the wavelength range of 1.65μm to 1.65μm. These results point to the suitability of the proposed HNDF-PCF to be used in the data communication system.

articleTitle: Improvement on level measurement & control of existing open drain caissons on fixed offshore platforms
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Majority of fixed offshore platforms in Brunei employ open drain caissons as a practical approach for collecting drains. It consists of a pipe submerged into the sea with an open bottom without any internals. Density and insolubility of the oil enables it to separate over time and settle atop of sea water within the open caisson and it is eventually removed via a pump through an oil level measurement and control system. Due to tidal variations in sea levels offshore, oil level monitoring and control of the open drain caissons alone is difficult. Majority of level measurement techniques employed no longer operate and/or do not give an accurate and reliable oil level indication. This leads to manual operation of the oil pump and in most cases, seawater is also pumped out along with the oil resulting in potential microbiologically induced corrosion on downstream systems. Inaction on this matter can potentially lead to, at worst case, loss of oil containment as the open drain caisson capacity is limited. This paper aims to study and provide recommendation to improve level measurement and control of open drain caissons on fixed offshore platforms whilst minimizing modification or re-design of the existing open drain caissons.

articleTitle: Fixed bed pyrolysis of biomass solid wastes for bio-fuels in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The fossil fuel demand is rising at an alarming rate causing environmental degradation. The use of alternative renewable sources of energy is the demand of the time. Biomass solid wastes are good options for this purpose. In the context of Brunei Darussalam sawdust is considered in this study. Sawdust is subjected to fixed bed pyrolysis for its conversion into bio-fuels. The pyrolysis system is designed and fabricated. It is a 50 cm long and 5 cm diameter fixed bed reactor with a 90 cm long condenser. Biomass is used to heat the pyrolysis reactor bed as well. The reactor and the condenser are made of stainless steel to cope up with high temperature and corrosive atmosphere. Sawdust is used for pyrolysis in the range of size of 10 to 50 mm. Experimental runs are conducted for 1 hour at different temperatures; 425°C, 500°C and 550°C respectively. The products obtained are char, oil and gases. The product yields are found to vary with temperatures; the liquid yield is the highest at the intermediate temperature. The char yield is found to decrease with temperature and the gas yield is observed to increase with temperature. The bio-fuels are characterized for some selective properties. The heating value of the solid bio-char is found to be 33.5 MJ/kg. The heating value of sawdust bio-oil is found to be 17.3 MJ/kg. The density of the oil is determined to be 950 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The pH value of the oil is found to be 1.66.

articleTitle: Comparison of the use of Herbst and SPI methods in identification of hydrological droughts
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Drought is an extended period of time with lack of rainfall causing considerable hydrological imbalance resulting in numerous hardships for all living beings. There are many methods developed to identify, analyse and assess droughts and their severity. This paper presents a study carried out to identify droughts in two drought prone districts in Sri Lanka using Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Herbst method. The SPI values were computed based on monthly, 3-monthly, seasonal and annual rainfalls, while monthly data were used in the application of the Herbst method. The computed drought periods were compared with the historical records on drought expenditures in the above two districts. Results indicate that the Herbst method is more suitable than the SPI method in identifying drought periods. Also, with the SPI method the use of seasonal or annual rainfall data is better compared to the use of monthly data.

articleTitle: Design of highly sensitive moisture sensor using hybrid core photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid porous core photonic crystal fiber (HPC-PCF) based sensor for sensing the moisture. In this design of HPC-PCF, octagonal cladding is composed of two circular rings having 40 air holes and hexagonal core is composed of 30 circular and one rectangular air holes. The whole simulation work of HPC-PCF has been carried out by Comsol Multiphysics software using finite element method (FEM). The various properties of HPC-PCF like sensitivity, confinement loss, effective area and nonlinearity are optimised by regulating the various geometrical parameters like pitch constant, air hole diameter and air filling fraction. This HPC-PCF displays the optimum relative sensitivity of 67% and confinement loss of 0.001dB/m at 0.8 μm pitch and 0.7 air filling faction of the cladding for 1.33μm absorption wavelength of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O molecule. This proposed design of HPC-PCF will keep momentous role for detecting moisture at different industrial products correctly.

articleTitle: Design and development of an autonomous agricultural drone for sowing seeds
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the design and fabrication of an autonomous agricultural drone for sowing seeds in the crop fields. In order to reduce the seeds sowing time, a seed sowing device has been specially developed and integrated with the quad-copter agricultural drone. The drone consists of a global positioning system (GPS) and an auto-pilot device, the flight path of which is controllable from the ground control station. The flying path can be programmed in the Mission-Planner software before the drone flight starts and can be altered if required. In addition, the agricultural drone is manually controllable using a long-range remote controller. It can fly under variable altitude where the maximum altitude is ∼ 500 meter. The drone can fly at a maximum speed of 14.76 km/hour. The maximum seeds sowing rate of 498 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/min is achieved for an altitude of 5 meter. At this seeds sowing rate, the mode value of seeds' distance is ∼ 2.5 cm. We can control the seeds sowing rate by controlling various operational modes of the seeds sowing device. The proposed agricultural drone will reduce the seeds sowing time significantly and contribute towards the automation of the agricultural sector.

articleTitle: Bio-fuels production through co-pyrolysis of biomass solid waste: A review
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: There are abundant sources of biomass solid wastes, for example, agriculture and industrial wastes that can be further utilized as renewable sources of energy. This can be done through the implementation of pyrolysis technique — the thermochemical conversion process of carbonaceous solid wastes into liquid, gas and solid products which may be used as alternative fuels or value-added materials. However, direct pyrolysis sometimes is not suitable especially for biomass with high moisture and ash content which requires upgrading. Hence, Co-pyrolysis which involves more than one feedstock at a time is expected to be able to improve the characteristics of bio-fuels, such as reduced oxygenated compounds, increased bio-oil yield and better calorific value. In this review, the main aim is to summarize recent evolution of co-pyrolysis research to investigate the principles and parameters affecting the process in the reactor as well as the yield and quality of the co-pyrolytic products. The parameters include feedstock, blending ratio, heating rate, temperature and type of reactor. This paper also considers the synergetic effect existing in co-pyrolysis through the extent of contact between feedstock and their effect on bio-fuels production. Catalytic co-pyrolysis as an emerging technique for high grade bio-oil will also be reviewed.

articleTitle: Challenges and opportunities of solid waste management in Bandar Seri Begawan
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)

authors.preferredName: Abdul Mu'ein bin Haji Adi Marhain
Asmaal Muizz Sallehhin Bin Hj Mohammad Sultan
authors.firstName: Asmaal Muizz Sallehhin Bin Hj Mohammad

abstract: Solid waste management has always been a global concern and continuous development of Brunei Darussalam's consumption patterns will change causing more complicated waste streams. This study investigates the waste stream in Bandar Seri Begawan (BSB) to identify the challenges and opportunities of solid waste management. This study is based on mixed research method approach integrating both quantitative and qualitative research methods. Qualitative information was obtained from in-depth interviews with municipal authorities and relevant departments and stakeholders with varying roles in the solid waste management system. Quantitative data gathered by questionnaire survey were conducted on the household and individual level within the project study area. The results from the survey indicates that 56.7% of the respondents have waste collection services provided by the Government and/or the private sector whilst the remaining 43.3% of respondents do not have such services. Out of the 56.7% of respondents with waste collection services, 92.2% are only provided with a single bin to store their waste whilst the remaining 7.8% are provided with segregated bins. In order for successful waste reduction strategies to be implemented in BSB, there must be an existing market for recyclable materials.

articleTitle: Planar and network spatial analyses of road traffic accidents — A review of methods and tools
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Developed and developing countries are observing increasing rate of road traffic accident (RTA) and they are investing in efforts trying to reduce the frequency and severity of RTA. Extensive research has been going on to develop methods to analyse historical RTA data using GIS tools to identify and rank RTA hotspots. This helps in prioritising expenditure distribution on road maintenance at road sections identified as RTA hotspots. The aim of this paper is to critically review some of the planar and network spatial analyses in RTA hotspot identification. The planar spatial analyses reviewed in this paper are one global statistical approach — Global Moran's I and three local statistical approaches — Local Anselin Moran's I, planar Kernel Density Estimation and Getis-Ord GI∗. These geostatistical approaches are embedded in ESRI ArcMAP analyst extension tools. The network spatial analyses reviewed in this paper are two tools based on network Kernel Density Estimation — SANET and KDE+. A new addition is a network-based approach that accounts for RTA frequency, severity and socioeconomic costs — Spatial Traffic Accident Analysis (STAA). After review, it is found that network spatial analyses are more preferred to planar spatial analyses for RTA hotspot analysis (HSA) on or along a road network.

articleTitle: Quantitative analysis of marine debris along the sea beaches of Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Debris along the sea beaches is a global concern and requires urgent attention from researchers and policy makers as it affects tourism, ecosystem and human health. Brunei Darussalam has 161 km long coast along South China Sea and continuous presence of debris is a growing concern. This pioneer study involves selection of four different beaches based on tourism activities and proximity to rivers in Brunei Darussalam. The debris was collected and analysed physically. The collected samples were categorized by number, weight, size and colour. By number, large amount of plastic (91.46%) was found on all four beaches. However, on the basis of weight, metals were the leading (41.6%) followed by plastic (37.62%). As most abundant type of debris was plastic, so it was then further classified on the basis of size and colour. Most of the materials found on these beaches were the result of tourism activities, but the contribution of debris by waterways is also significant. Although there were some signs of debris from neighbouring countries, but these were rare and mostly the debris collected was from local sources.

articleTitle: The toughness, strength, and thermal properties enhancement of toughened polyamide 6 nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Polyamide 6 (PA6)/ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA)/sepiolite nanocomposite was prepared in order to modify the properties of the PA6 matrix. The PA6/EVA blend and PA6/EVA/sepiolite nanocomposites were prepared using a twin screw extruder and injection molding machine. The effect of EVA concentrations (0–40 wt%) on the mechanical properties of PA6/EVA blends and the effect of sepiolite content (2–8 phr) on the mechanical, thermal and morphological properties of PA6/EVA/sepiolite nanocomposites were investigated. The PA6/EVA blend at a ratio of 80/20 was found as an optimum blend ratio based on its balanced mechanical properties and was used to prepare the nanocomposites. The tensile properties of PA6/EVA/sepiolite nanocomposites were increased until 6 phr of sepiolite content then decreased after that. The thermal stability of PA6/EVA/sepiolite nanocomposites improved with an increase in initial degradation temperature (T10%) and percentage of char residue. The morphological analysis concluded that well dispersion of sepiolite in nanocomposites was observed at the lower contents (2–6 phr) and sepiolite agglomeration occurred at higher content. The particle size of the EVA domain is one of the main factors that affected the properties of nanocomposites.

articleTitle: Onset fire detection in video sequences using region based structure from motion for non-rigid bodies algorithm
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Onset of fire detection plays a vital role in order to prevent spreading of fire to dangerous situations. Use of image processing can achieve significantly fast results in early fire detections. However, color and edge detection image processing techniques fail to accurately detect and identify events like the onset of fire in video sequences. To detect and identify fires by using video sequences we propose a technique using region based and a new three steps search based algorithm (NTSS) and structure from motion (SFM) technique. In this paper, we are proposing an algorithm known as SFM for non-rigid bodies (SFM-NRB) algorithm. In this algorithm, we calculate a randomness figure using region wise object boundary to differentiate fire from none fire events in 9 designated locations of the field of view of the camera. The result shows that the proposed algorithm is able to detect the onset of fire within 29 frames (within 1 sec) of the onset of fire. In future it can be further improved by using a high frame rate video cameras and multi sensor detection techniques.

articleTitle: 40 Gb/s photonic WDM transmitter design simulation and analysis
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Optical communication system has been studied in the past few decades due to its potential to mitigate the demand of the future state-of-the-art computing system. In this work, we proposed a 4-channel wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) transmitter design based on silicon photonics microring resonator. The radius variation method has been implemented in this design using a reference ring size of 1.00um. A comprehensive analysis of the proposed transmitter design has been carried out using the resonance analysis, spectral analysis, maximum number of channels as well as the transient response. Each channel was injected with 10Gbit/s random digital bit information which gives a total of 40Gbit/s of data transmission for the proposed WDM transmitter design.

articleTitle: Assessment of various methods to remove pathogen from raw water to meet who standard for domestic consumption
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This study was performed to evaluate the microbiological effectiveness of four commonly used Household Water Treatment (HWT) technologies like Mineral Pot Filters (MPF), Chlorination, Ultra Violet (UV) Radiation, and Coagulation and Sedimentation. Controlled laboratory experiments were conducted with two types of test waters with E.coli concentration greater than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> CFU/100 mL according to WHO guidelines. The experimental results showed that the four HWT technologies can be classified as Highly Protective (yielding a microbial log10 reduction value (LRV) greater than 4) according to WHO guidelines. For coagulation and sedimentation, increased alum dosage rendered several unwanted physico-chemical properties to the treated water. Coagulation and sedimentation can be classified as Protective (yielding a LRV of 2–4) for alum dose up to 26 mg/L and Highly Protective for alum dose greater than 26 mg/L. MPFs from two brands used in this experiment showed varying filtration rates but exhibited similar microbial efficiency with a LRV greater than 4. Chlorination with a dose of 0.02 mg/L with a contact period of 20 minutes yielded Highly Protective results and for UV radiation, 30 minutes of exposure time for a 6W (254 nm) UV lamp was required to produce Highly Protective results.

articleTitle: Reutilizing potentials of ablution water for sustainable living
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The existence of all living things is purely dependent upon the water presence, water covers around 70.9 % of earth surface but only 2.5% fresh water is available for the population of over 7 billion people, which is also fast depleting. According to ‘World Population Prospects 2015’ released by the United Nation (UN), Pakistan is among six of the 10 largest countries in the world whose population has been projected to exceed 300 million by 2050. At present, the country's population has been estimated to be around 190 million. Since water is a precious commodity hence it must be utilized wisely and judiciously. Pakistan is a Muslims majority country and it is obligatory for all Muslims to maintain prayer five times a day and it is prerequisite to perform ablution before prayer. Hence huge quantum of water is generated during ritual washing in the form of greywater from all over the Muslim world. The main objective of this study is to determine the potentials (quantity) of ablution water generated by the Muslims of Hyderabad City of Sindh province. A huge quantity of greywater is being generated from the mosques during ablution and mixing with polluted black water (wastewater). This mixed wastewater has various issues which includes load on conveyance system of sewage, chances of overtop the drains and ultimate burden on the wastewater treatment plants. It is observed that an average 7.44 liters is used to perform ablution by a person before each prayer. In this context, more than 2206 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> per day of greywater (Average) is being generated from almost 750 mosques of the Hyderabad. This water is relatively less polluted and can be reclaimed by simple physical treatment and disinfection process and reused for non-potable consumption.

articleTitle: Removal of various pollutants using constructed wetland with selected plants in humid tropical areas
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: A Horizontal Subsurface Flow (HSSF) system with selected tropic plants was studied during a 4-month period in Brunei Darussalam. This study evaluated the treatment efficiency of two local plants (Pandanus amaryllifolius and Nypa Fruticans) and one common plant (Imperata Cylindrica). Various forms of nitrogen (ammonia, nitrate, nitrite and Total Nitrogen), Total Phosphorus (TP), Total Oil and Grease (TOG), Total Petroleum Hydrocarbon (TPH), organic matter (BOD and COD) and microorganisms (E.Coli and Total Coliform (TC)) were tested regularly with standard method. The results show that the pollutant removal of the treatment efficiency of two local plants and one common plant for ammonia ranged from 23.81% to 87.82%, nitrate ranged from 19.64% to 56.67 %, nitrite ranged from 29.41% to 94.12%, Total Nitrogen ranged from 33.63% to 68.39%, TP ranged from 75.43% to 94.43%, TOG ranged from 16.92% to 95.27%, TPH ranged from 45.28% to 97.43%, BOD ranged from 27.50% to 90.35%, COD ranged from 80.49% to 90.76%, E.Coli ranged from 35.00% to 97.78% and TC ranged from 96.52% to 99.53%. Based on the experiments, it is found that both local plants (Pandanus amaryllifolius and Nypa Fruticans) are capable to remove varieties of pollutants in HSSF systems. Further experiments are required to study effect of additional factors such as different HRT and substrates.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of supersonic jet impingement
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The launch-pad is a vital ground platform from where a rocket or missile is launched. Continuous exposure to high pressure and temperature can have an effect on the launch-pad due to high temperature and shear stresses. The analysis of supersonic flow issuing from exhaust nozzle and its impact on launch-pad would help in understanding the heat experienced by launch-pad. The objective of this paper is to investigate the supersonic jet flow on the launch-pad and analyze the temperature and pressure experienced by it. Initial launch conditions of supersonic jet were simulated at varying distances from the ground. The simulation is done using ANSYS workbench and FLUENT.

articleTitle: GIS-based techniques to identify rainfall-induced flood risk zones (blue spots): A case study of Brunei River catchment
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Brunei continues to be inflicted by rainfall-induced floods that have been identified to be contributed by global climate change, increased population, developments, country's geography and her relative location in the Asia-Pacific region. By and large, floods cause detrimental effects on the country's social and economic health as well as damage to infrastructure and assets. Thus, it is becoming more imperative that a systematic study be conducted to identify the vulnerable locations (blue spots) in the flood-prone areas to help manage and mitigate the frequency and severity of floods respectively through engineering interventions. Using ArcMAP, the first goal of this paper is to determine the blue spots using planar spatial methods — Getis-Ord GI∗ statistics using aggregated data from 2010 to 2018 for Brunei River. The second goal is to use HEC-RAS two-dimensional unsteady flow analysis will be performed to model a flood event of 50-year return period to predict the flood depths and extents. Ultimately, the blue spot mapping helps many relevant departments to steer towards preparedness, protection and prevention strategies.

articleTitle: Consolidation behaviour of soft clay reinforced with crushed coir fibres
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Over the last few years, there has been a rise in research on the use of natural fibres as soil reinforcement materials due to an increase in awareness for sustainable and environmental friendly future. This paper presents findings from the ongoing research study on the possibility of the application of natural fibres as soil reinforcement. An experimental investigation was conducted at Universiti Teknologi Brunei to assess the consolidation properties of soft soil reinforced with natural fibres. The natural fibres used in this study is Coir fibres which can be locally obtained in Brunei Darussalam. These fibres were crushed and randomly mixed in clay with intermediate plasticity. The percentage inclusion of fibres was added at an increment of 0.5% to a maximum of 2.0%. Consolidation behaviour of these reinforced and unreinforced samples were observed and compared. The results indicated that various percentage inclusion of fibres affected the soil in terms of the coefficient of consolidation (cv), coefficient of permeability (k) and the soil's compressibility characteristics.

articleTitle: Pre-cracked RC beam strengthening with CFRP materials
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The application of CFRP materials for strengthening and rehabilitation of concrete structures has been spreading widely during the last two decades. Bonding failure of continuous fiber sheets is observed due to less adhesion with the concrete surface. Recently developed FRP strand sheet consists of individually hardened continuous fiber strands. This paper presents the shear strengthening capacity and failure modes of Pre-cracked Reinforced Concrete (RC) rectangular beams bonded externally with unidirectional Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) Composites. The study evaluates the efficiency of external strengthening of concrete members using CFRP strand sheets and compares this with the performance of continuous fiber sheets. Variables such as load vs deflection, end anchorage and number of CFRP U-strips applied (for shear retrofitting) are considered. Depending on the type of CFRP material and strengthening technique, beams strengthened for shear gave results close to or greater than control beam. Load capacity recovery of the beam specimens varied between 4–20% while deflection of the CFRP strengthened pre-cracked beam decrease by 8–23% (with respect to control beam) at ultimate load. In the ultimate loading condition mainly shear failure mode with concrete cover debonding are observed.

articleTitle: Effect of reduction in area in wire drawing process to micro structure and hardness of copper alloy wire
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Metal forming processes in the manufacturing field can be conducted by utilizing plastic deformation. In cold working process, forming is carried out at a temperature below the recrystallization temperature. Cold wire drawing is one of cold working processes. This current research is conducted to find out the micro structure change of material after wire drawing process and to investigate the effect of percentage reduction in area of wire to material's hardness. The experimental test specimen is a copper alloy wire. The copper alloy is widely used for power cables, roofing, piping and industrial machinery. This metal is drawn through inlet angles of 8° with various inlet diameters of 2.8, 2.4, and 2.2 mm respectively and outlet diameters of 2.4, 2.2, and 2.0 respectively. The grain shape and the hardness of copper alloy are investigated before and after wire drawing process. The experimental results after wire drawing process show that the grain shape was flatter than before wire drawing process. The result also shows that the greater the percentage reduction in area of the wire the higher the hardness of the material.

articleTitle: Performance of hybrid coir-glass/epoxy subjected to low velocity charpy impact
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Natural fibers are increasingly used as a reinforcement in fiber reinforced composite, due to their low cost, low density, sustainable availability compared to the traditional fibers. In addition, natural fibers are environmentally friendly materials. In this paper, low velocity charpy impact tests on coir, glass and hybrid coir-glass/epoxy were carried out. Hand lay-up method was used to fabricate the specimens with the dimensions of 50 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm. Impact specimens of a square, semi-circular and v-notch forms were fabricated and tested. Impact tests were conducted for a temperature range of −40°C to 40°C in intervals of 10°C. Effect of testing temperature, notch form, fibre volume fraction and span length to depth ratio on the impact energy were investigated. Failure mechanism of the fractured specimens was examined. Results show that impact energy of the composite specimens increased with increasing the temperature for the range of −40°C to 40°C. The glass/epoxy specimens with semi-circular notch form absorbed energy higher 19.22% and 26.83% than the v-notch and square notch form specimens. The impact energy of semi-circular notch glass/ epoxy specimens is found higher respectively 28.14% and 54.55% than that obtained from the hybrid coir-glass and coir/ epoxy specimens. The impact energy decreased significantly with increasing the span length to depth ratio from 6.88 to 11. The increase in the fibre volume fraction from 0.45% to 0.65% increased the impact energy of the tested specimens.

articleTitle: Water extend estimation over vegetated terrains in coastal area using multitemporal remote sensing data: A case study in Tumpat, Malaysia
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Detailed analysis of C-band Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images were collected to study water-level changes of coastal wetlands of Northern coast of Peninsular Malaysia. The intensity of SAR backscattering suggests that the dominant approach for mapping water extend in paddy field and wetland is backscattering threshold model. This solution can imply that SAR images can be used to estimate extend of water bodies with precise spatial details. The obtained results from SAR images indicate that water-extend changes over the time of study. The obtained results also show that the extend of water bodies is dynamic and spatially heterogeneous which is impossible to be mapped based on readings from sparsely distributed gauge stations. Moreover, by increasing the temporal frequency of satellites, chance of obtaining SAR observation and mapping a flood during a flood event and recession time rises.

Author Keywords: Remote sensing synthetic aperture water level

articleTitle: Use of semipermeable membrane devices (SPMD) for monitoring polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in Brunei's water reservoirs
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)

authors.preferredName: Amar Syahirah binti Hj Abd Murad
Nur Hakimah binti Hj Mohd Mansor

abstract: The presence of organic compounds in an aquatic environment can be a major pollution problem and hence, detection of these organic compounds which can be hazardous to both human and environmental health is important. In this study, semipermeable membrane devices (SPMD) are used as samplers to determine and evaluate the concentration of a group of organic compounds namely polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH, EPA priority 16). Two raw water abstraction areas which are located in different districts of Brunei are selected for a one-year sampling period between 2018 and 2019. SPMD are passive in-situ monitoring devices that can measure organic contaminants at a miniscule concentration in aqueous environment. This device consists of a thin film of lipid membrane with triolein enclosed in a thin-walled lay flat tubing made of low-density polymer. These characteristics make it an ideal sampler for the experiment. The SPMD-acquired concentration of PAHs accumulated in the SPMDs will be compared with those in water concentration taken from grab sampling technique. PAHs concentration will be determined and quantified by gas chromatography mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The use of SPMDs in this research provides a unique approach for Brunei Darussalam's water monitoring program due to the fact that such research and experiments have never been carried out before in Brunei Darussalam.

articleTitle: Prospect of renewable energy and its awareness in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Energy plays a vital role in our lives today. The main energy sources in Brunei are oil and natural gas. Brunei is the highest energy consumers in the ASEAN region with its consumption rate at 9293 kWh per capita in 2015, compared to Singapore's 8949 kWh per capita, and Malaysia's 4656 kWh per capita. This puts more strain on the available fossil fuel reserve. To increase the life span of the current fossil fuel reserve, it is therefore necessary to look for renewable energy and create awareness. The purpose of this paper is to find whether the implementation of renewable energy in Brunei can provide solutions to reduce problems on the over-reliance on fossil fuel. Based on our research and survey about awareness of renewable energy, this paper shows that renewable energy can contribute in terms of giving more sources of energy and a cleaner environment. There are economic, social, and environmental benefits in implementing renewable energy in Brunei. The type of renewable energy implemented depends on availability. In this regard more studies need to be conducted to support implementation of renewable energy.

articleTitle: An analysis of statistical correlation for downscaled precipitation data
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Among the few climate-related studies done in Brunei Darussalam, it is observed that previous research in related to the prediction of climate change scenarios using statistical downscaling method encounter difficulties in developing strong statistical correlations between precipitation and atmospheric parameters of Global Circulation Models (GCM). The statistical correlation between the observed precipitation (predictand) and the predictors were analysed that examined the correlation of 1, 2 and 3 days lagged precipitations and correlation with the data of surrounding GCM grids. Also, precipitation data were correlated with atmospheric data with and without rainfall (drydays). The results showed no strong statistical correlation exists between observed data with the reanalysed GCM data. The correlation coefficient between preditands with the predictors of National Centres for Environmental Prediction (NCEP) achieved a highest value of 0.18 and such data with high correlations was selected for rainfall prediction in Brunei Darussalam using multiple regressions.

articleTitle: Investigation for fluid flow rate for a tidal turbine
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: For a tidal and wind turbine, the maximum theoretical efficiency that the turbine can absorb from a moving fluid is 59.26%, this is known as the Betz Limit. However, developments have been made to increase the fluid flow rate to increase the power availability of the tidal and wind turbine. In this paper, 3 methods to increase the fluid flow rate have been investigated by using Solidworks Fluid Simulation to analyse the behaviour of the fluid as it passes through these devices. The change in velocity, pressure and the stability of the flow is examined in order to provide the most efficient method to further develop a tidal turbine.
