The power availability is calculated and compared to see the most effective design for the tidal turbine.

articleTitle: Improvement of grass cutting machine commonly used in Brunei
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The study involved a design and fabrication of a prototype power source for the brush cutter in which the two-stroke cycle petrol engine was replaced by a rechargeable battery powered electric motor. It can operate faster than the existing one when cutting the grass due to instantaneous torque produced. It was operated continuously more than an hour with a full charged as similar to the existing design. However, the mass of the prototype is 1.9 kg higher than the existing power source and the rotational speed was lower due to lower motor capacity (400W). The substantial advantages of this prototype brush cutter are being less noisy and vibration while operating.

articleTitle: 3D petrophysical modelling of bend conglomerate boonsville field Texas USA
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to carry out 3D petrophysical modelling for the reservoirs in Bend Conglomerate of Lower Atoka Stage of Boonsville Field to provide a good understanding of the hydrocarbon reserves of the targeted horizons. Property modelling was done by applying Stochastic technique and using Sequential Gaussian simulation (SGS) algorithm. The volumetric calculations for the targeted horizons shows that the deepest horizon MFS20 (Vineyard) has the highest Gas Initially In-Place (GIIP) and Recoverable gas (RGIIP) of 8.122 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> MSCF and 5.685 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> MSCF respectively. This study has showcased the use of the 3D static models as a tool to identify good hydrocarbon spots and aids in the identification of the karst collapses features, traps, anticlines, and spatial distribution of reservoir properties.

articleTitle: Potential of sewage sludge as energy recovery via gasification process
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Sewage sludge is a valuable resource and of considerable interest which has recently been exploited for its potential as an energy recovery. Sewage sludge gasification is an alternative and promising approach to find a continuous and reliable resource of disposal of the constant supply of sewage sludge, hence it is the attractive way of handling waste management. It is important to move towards the development of a sustainable energy solution to fulfil the present and future energy requirements and reduce the dependency on non-renewable resources. Therefore, the main aim of this study was to investigate the characteristics of sewage sludge collected from Gadong wastewater treatment plant to ensure its possibility for gasification conversion process. Proximate analysis, ultimate analysis, heating value and Energy Dispersive X-Ray Analysis (EDX) were performed. Results showed that the sewage sludge contains 2.70 wt. % moisture contents, 36.9 wt. % volatile matter, 63.0 wt. % ash contents and 7.77 wt. % fixed carbon with a heating value of 8.04 MJ/kg. Thermogravimetric and derivative thermogravimetric (TGA and DTG) analyses were examined to investigate the decomposition behaviour of sewage sludge under nitrogen (N2) and oxygen (O2) conditions at heating rates of 50.00°C to 900.00°C at 10.00°C/min for both conditions. The TG/DTG curves were compared to provide an inclusive description of the three different stages of thermal decomposition in all conditions. The overall conclusion based on experimental studies is that the characteristics and thermal analyses of sewage sludge are suitable as an energy recovery feedstock for the gasification process.

articleTitle: Effect of circulation flowrate and coolant temperature on progressive freeze concentration of roselle extract
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: In this research, progressive freeze concentration (PFC) has been applied in concentrating roselle extract. The aim of this research is to investigate the effect of two operating parameters which are the circulation flow rate and coolant temperature on the average freezing rate and average concentration efficiency of roselle extract. The process has been improved in this research as an automated PFC system was implemented to assist in concentrating the roselle extract. Analyses of the results illustrated that with a decrease in coolant temperature and increase in circulation flow rate, the average freezing rate showed an increment in trend. It has been found that average concentration efficiency increased as coolant temperature increased but decreased as circulation flow rate increased. From the analysis, it can be concluded that the highest average freezing rate for the effect of coolant temperature and circulation flow rate is 0.0112 min-1 and 0.25 min-1 at coolant temperature of −14°C and circulation flow rate of 3000 mL/min respectively. As for the average concentration efficiency, the highest value for the effect of coolant temperature and circulation flow rate has been recorded as 0.91 (at −6°C) and 1.02 (at 2200 mL/min) respectively.

articleTitle: Performance of empty and foam filled composite corrugated plates subjected to lateral loading
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Corrugated plates have been widely used in in various structural applications such as sandwich plate cores, roofing, bridges and buildings due to its higher strength and stiffness compared to the flat plates. In the present study, experimental work on the behavior of empty and foam filled composite corrugated plates under lateral loading was carried out. Woven roving [±45] glass and jute/epoxy materials were used for this investigation. Plates were of 200 mm length, 120 mm width and 20 mm height. Triangular and rectangular corrugation types were investigated. Polyurethane foam is used as a foam filler for the corrugated plates. Effect of the type of corrugation, material used, number of layers and the foam filler on the load-displacement relations were drawn and compared. Initial and mean load for the laterally crushed corrugated plates were included and compared. Total absorbed energy was obtained from the load-displacement graphs. Specific energy absorption has been plotted for the corrugated plates investigated. Failure modes for the corrugated plates were also investigated. Results show that the foam filled gkass/epoxy corrugated plates with rectangular corrugation absorbed energy higher 16.98% than the plates with triangular corrugation form. The four layers glass/epoxy corrugated plates supported load higher 33.15%, and 50.90% than the jute-glass and jute/epoxy corrugated plates respectively. Failure mechanism of the corrugated plates is influenced by the corrugation form and material used. The foam filled corrugated plates were more stable against buckling during the lateral loading compared to the empty corrugated plates.

articleTitle: Sonication assisted transesterification of Jatropha oil for the production of biodiesel: A kinetic study
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Fossil-based fuels are main sources for atmospheric pollution and global warming. Biodiesel is the most attractive alternative fuel to the fast depletion of fossil oil. Jatropha oil is renewable non edible oil with high percentage of free fatty acids (FFAs). It generally forms soap in the presence of alkali catalyst during the production of biodiesel. In order to overcome this problem, we attempted to produce biodiesel through two-step transesterification. In the first step 1 wt % sulfuric acid (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) in oil was used for transesterification of Jatropha oil at 60°C in the mixture of one part of acid free oil with six parts of methanol. The first step was carried out to reduce the FFAs content to a minimal value. In the second step Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH) catalyzed esterification was carried out at 60°C to convert FFA free Jatropha oil to biodiesel. Sonication at 20 KHz was used in both the steps. Sonication could help achieving intensive mixing of the reaction mixture during transesterification process. The conversion of biodiesel was estimated through hydrogen nuclear magnetic resonance. We could achieve in the first step 99% reduction of FFA followed by 92% conversion of resultant Jatropha oil to biodiesel in 45 min. The reaction rate constants k for transesterification were estimated at different temperatures and the rate equation was derived. We conclude that the two step transesterification is likely to be a most promising environment friendly method to convert Jatropha to biodiesel.

articleTitle: Empirical estimation of the rock strength of Walloon Coal measures, Surat Basin Australia using Sonic log
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The sonic velocity log has been used as an indicator for unconfined uniaxial rock strength (UCS) in many oil fields and underground mines. The relationship between the rock strength and the compressional, or p-wave, velocity as measured by the sonic log (DT) has been shown by various equations. Besides the DT, some equations have used other logs such as bulk density and total porosity. However, the quantitative estimation of the rock strength requires a good correlation between empirical calculations of UCS using p-wave velocity and the laboratory measurements of the uniaxial compressive strength (UCS). This paper uses the calibrations between McNally equation and mechanical tests in Bowen Basin, Queensland to estimate UCS in Surat Basin. The Jurassic Walloon Coal Measures with 200–300m thickness and up to 36 coal seams is the major coal measure in Surat Basin. Several thousand coal seam gas (CSG or coal bed methane, CBM, in the United States) wells have been drilled in Surat Basin and many future wells are planned to produce coal seam gas. This paper uses the sonic log to calculate UCS using McNally (1987) and Horsrud (2001) empirical equation and compares the rock strength in 132 wells from public data. The plot of the UCS values for the five major litho-stratigraphic units, Springbok Sandstone, Upper and Lower Juandah coal measures, Tangalooma Sandstone and Taroom Coal measures shows the various inter-burden rock competencies. The UCS estimation shows change in trend versus depth and variation between different stratigraphic units. These results can be used for better understanding of the sand production, well stability and open hole design for CSG wells in Surat Basin.

articleTitle: Induced voltage and current estimation on pipelines near high voltage transmission lines
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The highest magnitude of induced voltage on a pipeline is dangerous for utility operators. In this paper, the induced voltages and currents on the proposed realistic pipeline near 275 kV high voltage transmission lines along the Muara-Tungku highway in Brunei were calculated under steady-state and lightning conditions using a MATLAB-based software. For calculations, a uniform soil resistivity of 30Ω-m, 50Ω-m and 81 Ω-m and a load current of 1373A for the transmission lines were considered. The induced voltages on the pipeline were found to be 6.94 V, 6.09 V and 2.07 V for the centreline symmetric (ABC-ABC), partial-roll upper symmetric (ABC-BAC) and centre point symmetric (ABC-CBA) lines, respectively. In addition, the induced voltages and currents with different lightning conditions were calculated and its mitigation was also investigated. Furthermore, the induced voltage estimation was performed using various machine learning techniques and a high coefficient of determination was found in ensemble methods.

articleTitle: Acid treatment on thin film composite membrane support to enhance water flux in forward osmosis
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Membrane-based desalination has been extensively explored to expand the access to affordable and safe drinking water. In the recent decade, forward osmosis has emerged as an attractive alternative to conventional reverse osmosis desalination due to some advantages in terms of lower energy consumption and less susceptibility towards fouling. However, despite these benefits, overcoming low water flux remain a challenge. Acid treatment of membrane support has shown to impart some desired characteristics for membrane separation performance. Compared to the control membrane, the acid treated membrane showed an increase in water flux from 1.48 to 2.77 L/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>h (when active layer facing FS) and from 4.51 to 5.68 L/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>h (when active layer facing draw solution) while retained small reverse solute flux.

articleTitle: Remote sensing application in rainforest monitoring in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Remote sensing application has advances over the decades from primarily aerial photography to detection and measurement of energy patterns from different portions of the electromagnetic spectrum to obtain information of an area or phenomenon on the earth surface or near environmental surface to study the physical and chemical characteristics from distance. This is common and ideal in forest sector study particularly in monitoring of forest cover changes. These interrelated disciplines have succeeded to observe the changing patterns of the rainforest in Brunei Darussalam from the year 1990 to 2015 based on primary and secondary sources relative to Brunei Darussalam. The monitoring of rainforest cover with more than 90% accuracy using multi temporal Landsat images deduced the trend of forest cover change in Brunei Darussalam with 46% non-forest expansion; 27% forest conversion and 12% forest regeneration in 25 years. Relatively, health, safety and environmental (HSE) procedure; statistical data for non-wood forest products; recognition of the shared indigenous culture in Brunei in relation to Borneo, and; sustainable development is suggested to supplement the rainforest sustainability.

articleTitle: Structural studies of BaCe0.7Zr0.1Y0.1Pr0.1O3-δ perovskite for IT-SOFCs
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The BaCe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Pr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</inf>, a perovskite oxide type specimen has been synthesized for application in electrolyte for anode-supported protonic solid oxide fuel cell by the conventional solid state reaction in air at 1350°C for 8 hours. The X-ray diffraction (XRD) experiment and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) were done for structural analysis and Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA-DTA) has been performed for thermal and differential thermal characterization. Rietveld refinement of the XRD data has been performed by using FullProf software and single phase orthorhombic crystal structure with the Pbnm space group was confirmed. The TG/DTA scan was recorded under constant flow of Argon gas to understand the temperature dependent behaviour of the precursor which exhibits weight loss at 780°C. The SEM image of the pellet surface of the sample shows that the sample sintered at 1350°C was dense without any pore or crack. The structural properties of the sample showed that can be a good candidate as an electrolyte in solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs).

articleTitle: Convolutional neural networks for facial emotion recognition towards the development of automatic pain quantifier
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) has been one of the mainstream topics in the areas of computer vision. Numerous databases of facial expressions are available to the research community and are used as fundamental tools for the evaluation of a wide range of algorithms for FER. With the continuous evolution of deep learning in computer vision, FER has enticed many researchers within the area of Artificial Intelligence, applying powerful machine learnings to enhance the overall user experience in solving many real-world problems. In this study, we review the state of the art of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) as a computational model for image classification, accentuating the algorithmic structure and its functional impact. We implemented CNN building framework to validate a real-time system that is applied to automatically classify key human emotions: Angry, Disgust, Fear, Happy, Sad, Surprise, and Neutrality using FER2013 emotion datasets. The study showed that CNN model yields a high-efficiency result in achieving a high-level performance of automatically recognizing emotions from dynamic facial expressions. Our paradigm extends to the development of an artificially intelligent system capable of recognizing pain and its intensity and can diagnose a convincing and reliable outcome that speaks the same language from a medical perspective.

articleTitle: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) piezoelectric energy harvesting from rotary retracting mechanism: Imitating forearm motion
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper developed an effective energy harvesting device prototype design that make use of PVDF to convert kinetic energy from human kinetic movement (specifically in forearm) to electrical energy, ideally in real time. The energy harvesting device prototype consists of rotary retracting generator which imitating the forearm motion. Therein, by means of research in theoretically and experimentally study of energy harvesting are conducted and observed during inward and outward of forearm motions by using the rotary retracting mechanism. The design of PDVF film being attached to forearm are reviewed and LTC3588-2 chip were used to obtained DC power output result from the working energy harvesting device prototype. The harvested energy accumulated through power management circuit which were integrated in LTC3588-2 chip and increase during every cycle of rotating generator. One cycle would generated about 0.010V. After 6 minutes of operating the piezoelectric energy harvesting system, the system had accumulated 0.488V.

articleTitle: Wind generation modelling in LDC based generation planning models — A case study of omani power sector with WASP-IV
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Most of the popular and widely used software tools for strategic planning of generation expansion are based on load duration curve technique, which disregards the chronology of the events; hence intermittent generation resources are not properly modelled. In addition, in such software the environmental costs of the power plants are not embedded within the optimization process but calculated after the "optimal" plan is made. This paper describes how to model the intermittent resources or non-dispatchable technologies such as wind in these kinds of tools that are based on load duration curve models. In addition, the paper describes how to model environmental costs within the fuel cost of each technology so that a truly optimal generation mix is found. As a case study, the paper concentrates on finding the optimum generation capacity expansion plans for the Main Interconnected System (MIS) of Oman using WASP-IV software, which is based on load duration curve technique.

articleTitle: Laboratory investigation of the microbiological performance of ceramic water filters as household water treatment technology
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Ceramic Water Filter (CWF) is a widespread household water treatment (HWT) technology in urban and rural areas of developing countries like Bangladesh. However, information regarding the microbiological performance of CWF is rare. A 23 weeks study was undertaken aiming to evaluate the microbiological performance of commercially available CWFs in Bangladesh under laboratory controlled environment according to WHO protocol. A total of 24 filters from three well-known brands were purchased and the removal performance of E.coli bacteria, MS-2 bacteriophage virus and Clostridium perfringens spores were evaluated using two types of challenged waters. Results showed that filter performance declined with the increasing filtration period. The filters were found moderately effective but inconsistent in reducing E.coli (1.03–2.15 log<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> reduction), MS2 (0.52–1.52 log<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> reduction) and less effective against C. perfringens spores (0.50–1.06 log<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> reduction). Also the devices can effectively reduce turbidity (> 98% removal) and color (> 90% removal). In complying WHO guideline, only one brand achieved protective target in few cases. The findings of this study is very much to a study in Cambodia, however more scientific performance data is needed to confirm its reliability.

articleTitle: Investigation of energy usage in the university buildings
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper presents the investigation on electrical energy usage in two academic blocks, A and F in the Universiti Teknologi Brunei. The energy usage has been measured for a period of seven months with energy meters located in the switchboard. From the measured data, it has been found that 69% of the electrical energy is consumed by air-conditioning system while the other 31% is consumed by the lighting systems and miscellaneous sockets. From the connected load, it has been found that the air-conditioning equipment in block F is not fully utilized whereas in block A, it is fully utilized. The lighting intensity requirement for both the blocks are found to comply with the standard values. The connected air-conditioning loads per person has been found to be higher compared with the standard requirement.

articleTitle: Thermal-based wavelength reconfigurable digital electro-optic D-type flip-flop
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the design of a thermally reconfigurable/tunable operating wavelength of the digital electro-optic D-type flip-flop. The design of the D flip-flop is based on the silicon micro-ring resonator as its core component. The optical modulation technique incurred in the micro-ring resonator utilizes the carrier-injection forward-biased PIN ring waveguide. Micro-heaters are applied to the proposed design with controlled heat generation in order to modulate the operational wavelength, thus allowing the proposed design to operate at varying wavelength. This work proceeds with the simulation and time-varying analysis of the proposed design at the data rate of 1Gbps, and the clocking speed of 5Gbps. Two different operating wavelengths of 1550nm and 1552nm are used to show that the proposed design is wavelength reconfigurable via thermal tuning.

articleTitle: Bridging the gap between water potential and water utilization for Bazkhando weir command
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: With depletion of water resources and increase in water demand Government of Pakistan has moved forward towards construction of small dams/weirs, Bazkhando recharge weir being one of such projects. So far the purpose of construction of this weir is to capture the catchment runoff during the monsoon and recharge the aquifer for human and livestock consumption in command area of this project. Due to the lack of comprehensive water management plan, its implementation and subsequent development in the project area, it is witnessed that scope of water use is limited compared to its potential. So it is urgent need to propose and implement various viable options for Bazkhando command area development to boost and optimize the use of the stored water for achievement of optimal and sustainable benefits. This article aims at bridging this gap between water potential and it's utilization for improving socio-economic conditions of the living community and making the project productive and proficient by proposing a comprehensive command area development plan in line with principles of IWRM for Bazkhando weir command.

articleTitle: Synthesis and characterization of La9.95Ba0.05Si5.8Zn0.2O26.775 co-doped lanthanum silicate electrolyte for intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Apatite-type lanthanum silicates have been successfully produced as the electrolyte materials for the intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells. In this paper, La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9.95</inf>Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5.8</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">26.775</inf> co-doped lanthanum silicate electrolyte has been prepared by the conventional solid-state reaction method to investigate the structural, morphological and electrical properties of the electrolyte. The oxyapatite electrolyte has been characterized by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Hexagonal apatite structure of La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9.95</inf>Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5.8</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">26.775</inf> with space group P6<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/m formed as the major phase after sintered at 1600°C for 8 hours. articleTitle: Leaning to lean for resource management
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Resource management in construction projects has many difficulties. Realizing the importance of resource value, identifying the resource value streamline and continuous flow, and adopting the "pull" approach along with perfection can overcome certain difficulties. A better understanding of lean principles through the thought processes and decision making can yield benefit realisation with production capabilities in project environments. This research is aimed at capturing the practitioner perceptions on enabling resource management practices through fundamental lean principles: value, value stream, flow, pull, and perfection. A questionnaire survey was conducted in India. In this survey, information and space have been found to be essential to ensure the performance of critical factors for direct and supportive works. Information and space resources can influence other resources. About one-third of the respondents mentioned that information influences cycle time, lead time, changes, take time, and work in process. The look-ahead plan focuses on eliminating resource constraints to smooth workflow. Root causes derived from raising questions and iterative plan-do-check-act cycle enable continuous improvement process. Lean thinking in resource management can support the effective and efficient use of resources in construction projects.

articleTitle: Investigation on energy extraction methods for EEG channels selection in improving common spatial pattern
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Motor imagery on EEG signals are widely used in brain computer interface (BCI) system with many interesting applications. However, it is not easy to interpret motor imagery EEG signal due to non-stationary and noisy features of the signal. In this paper, we investigate three different techniques of energy calculation as a part of energy extraction methods including L2-norm, leverage score, and absolute Z-score. This BCI framework use CSP as motor imagery signal feature extraction method and extreme learning machine (ELM) to classify the features of motor imagery signal. In general, the investigated framework has proved that the energy extraction methods can improve the performance of CSP. Also, an effective EEG channel selection provides better performance in terms of classification accuracy. In general, the proposed energy extraction methods can offer up to 21% performance improvement in accuracy and 86% reduction number of channels as compared to the original CSP.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamics modelling of a river with mangrove forests
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The existence of mangroves produces high resistance to flow which affects water level and current in rivers. For this reason, it is crucial to consider the flow resistance factor associated with mangrove vegetation in river hydrodynamic models. This paper describes the numerical simulation of hydrodynamics of the Brunei River, a tidal river with extensive mangrove intertidal zones using MIKE 21 based on two different model representations of mangroves: 1) a model applying spatial Manning's m coefficient between cells enclosing mangroves and main river, and 2) a model applying uniform Manning's m coefficient which indicates the absence of mangroves. The calibration and verification mean absolute error (MAE) results indicate that the model with varying resistance distribution captures satisfactorily the water levels and current patterns of the Brunei River covered with mangroves. Based on these findings, the hydrodynamics are properly understood within the Brunei River and the calibrated model can be coupled with water quality modelling to assess water quality of a river with mangrove forests.

articleTitle: Characterization of biomass solid wastes for bio-fuel production in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Brunei Darussalam aims to achieve at least 10% of energy generation from renewable resources by the year 2035 to reduce the impact of climate change and reliance on fossil fuel reserves. Brunei with its vast number of rainforests and rising agriculture sector should take advantage of utilizing biomass solid wastes as an alternative energy source. In addition, with the growth of population, there is a rise of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) generated creating disposal and pollution problems. Pyrolysis has been known as an effective method to convert biomass solid wastes into bio-fuels which can be used as alternative fuels or value-added products. The characterization study of the biomass solid wastes is an important step to assess the properties of the feedstock. This allows for the selection of the suitable feedstock pyrolysis system and for the proper pyrolysis system design. In this paper, selective characterization investigations have been conducted on saw dust, poultry waste and waste tyre. The characterization study includes the determination of physical properties (particle size and bulk density), proximate analysis (moisture content, ash content, volatile matter and fixed carbon), Higher Heating Value and elemental analysis Carbon, Hydrogen, Nitrogen, Oxygen and Sulphur content, (CHNOS) analysis.

articleTitle: GIS-based forest fire risk assessment for the Belait district
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Widespread forest fires have been a regular event in the Southeast Asian region particularly during dry periods. Brunei Darussalam, as one of the Southeast Asian countries, loses hundreds of hectares of forests every year, and more. Fire behaviour varies under different conditions and the nature of the forests. The degrees of challenge and impact posed by fires differ with types of forest cover and soil. This paper therefore attempts to assess fire risk in the Belait District by considering different fire contributory factors. This task was assisted by the application of a Geographical Information System (GIS). In this study, factors such as forest cover type, soil types, distance from road, proximity of settlements and population, are derived and classified for the study area. A fire risk map was then developed using Analytical Hierarchical Process (AHP) and Suitability Analysis tools in GIS. The outcomes showed that the high fire risk areas are at the northern part of the district and aligned with the shoreline, whereas low risk areas are found at the lower part of the district. The result also demonstrates the potential of integrating AHP and suitability analysis tools for fire risk assessment studies.

articleTitle: Physico-chemical analysis, classification of ground water, and impact of water quality on the health of people in Khushab City, Pakistan
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Ground water quality was evaluated by analysing physico-chemical parameters e.g. pH, Electric Conductivity (EC), Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), Total Hardness (TH), Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, Mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and CI" from fifty sites within the urban settlements of Khushab City, Pakistan. Distribution of the contaminants and their impact on public health was also analysed. Water samples were classified on the basis of TDS and TH. Arc GIS software was used to plot the spatial distribution of contamination. Results showed that pH value ranged between 6.8 and 8.7, EC between 260 and 10290μS/cm, TDS between 179 and 9410mg/l, Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+2</sup> between 1.2 and 11.8mg/l, Mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+2</sup> between 0.3 and 39.4mg/l, TH between 6.23 and 216.86mg/l, CI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup> between 0.3 and 344.7. Water quality was then correlated with the health condition of the residents which demonstrated water borne diseases like Hepatitis, Cholera, Gastro, and Kidney stone etc. is common in the study area.

articleTitle: Investigation of efficient use of energy in the industrial sector of Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Brunei Darussalam continues to be dominated by the use of oil and gas as its main source of energy production. However, with the recent decline in oil and gas production coupled with the decrease in the oil and gas prices in the international market, the government of Brunei Darussalam faced a number of challenges. To overcome the challenges, the government of Brunei Darussalam has taken few initiatives: a decrease in the national energy intensity by 25% in the year 2030, diversification of the energy mix through a concerted effort, and promoting the alternative and renewable energy sources for power generation. From the available literature, the GDP per kilogram of oil equivalent for the world is tabulated. Comparison of the energy efficiency is made both at national and international level with a selected SME of Brunei Darussalam. Recommendations are provided to improve the energy efficiency of the SME.

articleTitle: A water quality database for Brunei — The case of Bukit Barun and Layong
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)

authors.preferredName: Nur Hakimah Binti Haj Mohd Mansor

abstract: This project aims to generate a water quality database of Brunei Darussalam which previously did not exist. Data populated in the database consist of raw water analysis (Bukit Barun, Layong) and rainfall data from the years 2014 to 2016. The database structure was built and populated. To demonstrate the suitability of such database a correlation analysis of several water parameters i.e. pH, turbidity, colour unit, chloride, fluoride, aluminium and daily rainfall was performed. Previous studies have found that Brunei Darussalam soils are partly composed of acid sulphate soil, hence this database aids to investigate how acid sulphate soils can affect the water quality in Brunei. The highest positive correlation resulted from the turbidity-colour unit correlation (r=0.67), followed by turbidity-aluminium correlation (r=0.44). In contrast, notable negative correlations include pH-rain correlation (i=− 0.40), pH-Colour unit correlation (r=−0.39) and pH-aluminium correlation (r=−0.34). The result of the aluminium-pH correlation further indicates that leaching of aluminium and possible other toxic elements from the soils increases with the effect of low pH. The database will be a useful tool for future decision making and analysis for the country.

articleTitle: Alkalinity and strength properties of concrete containing macro silica and ground granulated blast furnace slag
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: As the industrial by-products are continually increasing, and no strategic waste management scheme is put in place in developing communities, an effective solution is being sort through the use of industrial rejects in concrete production. This study evaluates the alkalinity and strength properties of concrete containing macro silica and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS). Varying proportions of GGBS and macro silica were used as partial replacement of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) and river sand in concrete respectively, while other materials including granite and water content were kept constant. It was observed that the alkalinity of concrete is not affected by the modification of materials in the concrete as performed in this study. Higher 28 days strength properties, comparable to the reference concrete, was achieved when 10% macro silica and 50% GGBS were used as partial replacement of sand and OPC respectively.

articleTitle: Investigation on mechanical properties of friction stir welding of 2 mm thick aluminium alloy sheet
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The objective on the research was to investigate the mechanical properties and microstructure of joining between identical aluminium alloys of AA6061-T6 and AA1100 by using friction stir welding (FSW) process. Due to the unstable stirring process of welding, microhardness test was conducted to measure the hardness distribution across the weld nugget. The mixing of two distinct materials was influenced by tool rotation speed. Therefore, microstructure analysis was carried out to investigate the grain size and shape. At the heat affected zone (HAZ), the grain size of AA6061-T6 increased, on the while those of AA1100 decreased. In the weld nugget, a hook defect in the aluminium alloy joining was detected. By using monotonic tensile load, the different weld line directions were observed with the expansion in tool rotation. The joints failure was consistent on the area of AA1100 series. Furthermore, two specimens were investigated, one through the 1xxx aluminium series and the other through 6xxx aluminium series. Inspection of the weld nugget hardness indicates the non-homogenous material intermixing during the stirring process that is confirmed by the results of microhardness measurement.

articleTitle: Degradation of pollutants on ground surfaces of paved urban areas
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: A lab-based experiment study was conducted to investigate the degradation of pollutants on pavement under the natural environment condition of dry days. In this experiment, waste water with high concentrations of pollutants was seeded on specially made concrete plots which represent impervious urban surfaces to avoid heterogeneity of pollutants dispersion on urban land surfaces. Simulated rainfall was employed to wash the pollutants off the plots after various antecedent dry periods (ADP). This can eliminate variability of unpredictable rainfall pattern. Pollutants degradation analysis was derived from the event mean concentrations (EMCs) of runoff collection obtained during the different ADPs ranged from 1 d–10 d, consecutively with one-day gap intervals. From the experiments, significant temporal variation was found for BOD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>, TOG and TC. BOD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> build-up was observed during the first 6–8 days of the dry period and degraded thereafter. TOG continually degrades over ADP while TSS, NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and TPH showed insignificantly influenced by the length of ADP. No significant difference in the effect of degradation rates was observed between the thinner (2 cm) and thicker (5 cm) study plots. This suggested that the depth of impervious materials is not the influential factor when the surface has extremely low in both permeability and porosity.

articleTitle: Tube shear wall interaction of high rise building and influence of damper on its dynamic behavior
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: A tubular frame is a structural system that is used for high rise building to obtain greater height and by adding shear wall the building can go even higher. With the development of new construction materials and procedure the strength of the construction material has been raised several times. As a result of this the members of a tubular building are becoming slender day by day causing rendering problems of vibration and oscillation under earthquake and wind loads. The remedy to this kind of problems may be either to use shear wall or/and bracing or by the use of damper. In this study the dimension of shear wall is varied and effectiveness of the structure is observed under lateral loading. The study reveals that by properly selecting shear wall dimensions and damper parameters a tubular structure can be made more effective and the dynamic response of the building can be controlled and kept within tolerable limit.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of Zn doped BaCe0.7Zr0.15Y0.15O3-δ thin film proton conducting materials for IT-SOFC
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Considering good chemically stable and high proton conductive materials is the key to develop proton conducting solid oxide fuel cells operating at intermediate temperature. Wet chemical sintering route offers the opportunity to fabricate very thin electrolyte films than traditional powder-based materials. A novel method is presented for the preparation of a thin film proton conducting electrolyte for SOFC application. The present work deals with the fabrication of 5 % Zn doped BaCe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</inf> (BCZYZn15) thin film electrolyte. Electrolyte materials were prepared by an acetate-methoxy ethanol solution method and examined by multilayer (4, 6, 8 times) coating on silicon and anode (NiO-BaCe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</inf>) substrate at different temperatures. A thin, dense, crack free BCZYZn15 electrolyte film was successfully obtained on a dense anode by spin coating. Post-mortem analysis by scanning electron microscope (SEM) revels that no crack on 6 layers coating at 1100°C. Furthermore, this work shows that, Zn doped BaCe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</inf> dense thin film could be good electrolyte for IT-SOFC.

articleTitle: A review of planning guidelines and standards for earthwork development near slopes in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Brunei Darussalam receives an average annual rainfall of about 3200 mm and is susceptible to slope failures. Slope failures generally occur and are reported during the periods of heavy rainfall. Official figures indicate 937 reported slope failures occurred during the period from 2011 to 2016 and 86% of these cases in Brunei-Muara District. Land development is the main cause and the Ministry of Development has hence prepared the "Planning Guidelines and Standards for Earthwork Development" to serve as a guide in processing applications for earthwork and land development within the Environmentally Sensitive Area (ESA). The guideline attempts to establish the applicable principles and to rationalise the adopted processes according to a set routine practice. Effective slope design guidelines help to ensure the safety of new structures built at locations with high risk of slope failure. This paper critically reviews this guideline of Brunei Darussalam with the aim to identify the areas that require further research, elaboration or refinement. The review is facilitated by comparison of similar and well-established guideline from Hong Kong. Preliminary analysis identified several areas that require attention such as: 1) desk and field study; 2) parameter determination; 3) accounts of drainage and pore water pressure distribution; 4) recommendation of modelling for critical cases; and 5) definite framework of practices, monitoring and observation during post-implementation phase.

articleTitle: Evaluation of petrophysical parameters and reservoir potential of Boka bil and Bhuban formations of Surma Basin, Bangladesh: A case study of Rashidpur gas field using well log
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Petrophysical analysis of both the Boka Bil and Bhuban Formations are studied and evaluated using the conventional well log data of five different wells of Rashidpur Gas Field located in the Surma Basin, Bangladesh. The main lithology of the targeted formations composed of sandstone and shale as identified by the various types of cross plots. The quantitative parameters were analysed using the software called Interactive Petrophysics (IP-2013). The shale volume, porosity and water saturation for the productive hydrocarbon pay zones are limited by some cut-off values of 50%, 10% and 50%, respectively, which were chosen to determine the best pay zones. The iso-parametric contour maps for the average reservoir parameters; such as average porosity, shale volume, water saturation, hydrocarbon saturation, net reservoir and net pay were also illustrated. From the present study, the presence of substantial amount of hydrocarbons and the pay zones within the Boka Bil and Bhuban Formations reveal that the studied formations exhibit reservoir potential. The study also affirms that there is good indication of accumulation of gas in the Rashidpur Field which may lead to locate new drilling sites and subsequent production within the vicinity of the selected wells.

articleTitle: Characterisation of various tropical rainforest wood species as potential feedstocks for biofuel production
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Wood biomass is a source of renewable and sustainable energy that is widely spread in the world and presents a lower cost alternative to fossil fuel. Biomass resources may include wood residues produced from various wood activities (e.g. wood-work, house or furniture making etc.), hence it is considered as municipal solid wastes. Wood residues can be used or recycled for generating electricity, heat, and biofuels. In this paper, chemical compositions of 10 different types of tropical rainforest wood species found in Brunei Darussalam were studied for their potential use as feedstocks for biofuel production. The chemical compositions of the wood species in terms of extractives, holocellulose, lignin, moisture and ash were determined by using the wood analytical method. The elemental composition was investigated using Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX). The characterisation results suggested that Alan Batu species has an absolute potential for biofuel production due to its higher lignin content (41.1%), lower moisture (0.8%) and ash content (0.0%).

articleTitle: Minimization of trafic congestions using a traffic adaptive model
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: In the last decade, cities in Asia have undergone rapid expansion and population growth driven by higher job opportunities, better healthcare and education. Changes in the city's population appear to have significant impact on transport and road energy use. Residents in cities are increasingly dependent on commuting by private car due to the rise in household income. Traffic congestion and air pollution has highlighted the need to make traffic management in cities smarter. This paper compares two methods of controlling traffic congestion at a single intersection using fixed and adaptive traffic light algorithm. The adaptive algorithm uses TSTMA and is based on the Markov-Kendall queuing theory model. At present traffic light system in Brunei Darussalam is assigned to be static, i.e., traffic light signal changes are fixed. The aim of this paper is to demonstrate how adaptive traffic light system can be used to help minimize Brunei's traffic congestion during peak hour.

articleTitle: CFD analysis on MHD flow of two-fluid model for blood rheology in constricted arteries
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This computational study analyses the pulsatile flow of blood in a narrow artery with mild asymmetric stenosis, treating the blood flow as two-layered model with the suspension of all the erythrocytes in the core layer region as Casson fluid and the cell depleted plasma in the peripheral layer region as Newtonian fluid. Finite difference method is employed to solve the resulting system of non-linear partial differential equations along with a set of initial and boundary conditions. Explicit finite difference scheme is derived for velocity profile, flow rate, wall shear stress and longitudinal impedance to flow. It is noted that skin friction and longitudinal impedance to flow increase with the increase of yield stress, Hartmann number and stenosis depth. The aforementioned fluid behaviour is reversed to the velocity profile and flow rate when these parameters increase. It is found that the longitudinal impedance to flow for the two-fluid Casson model is considerably lower than that of the single-fluid Casson model.

articleTitle: Investigation of bushing performance using silicon carbide material
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of insulation performance of undoped silicon carbide in high voltage equipment (bushing) via COMSOL Multiphysics simulation software. The bushing diagram was drawn by actual dimension given by industrial manufacturing data. Then, it is simulated using COMSOL Multiphysics software to calculate the electric potential and electric field. The outer surface of the bushing was contaminated with sodium chloride and simulated. The electric field and potentials are compared for both clean and contaminated conditions. Finally, the results were summarized.

articleTitle: Electrochemical and structural characterization of BaCe0.7Zr0.15Y0.1Zn0.05O3-δ as an electrolyte for SOFC-H
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: As a potential electrolyte for proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC-Hs) and to get better protonic conductivity and stability, zinc doped BCZY material has been found to be promising. In this study, we report a new composition of proton conductors BaCe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</inf> (BCZYZn10) which was investigated using XRD, SEM and conductivity measurements. Rietveld refinement of the XRD data revel a cubic perovskite structure with Pm-3m space group. Rietveld analysis of BaCe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</inf> shows the unit cell parameter is a = 4.3582(7) Å. Scanning electron microscopy images shows that the grain sizes are large and compact which gives the sample high density and good protonic conductivity. The total conductivity in wet atmosphere is significantly higher than that of dry condition and the conductivity was found to be 0.004032 Scm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and 0.00164 Scm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> at 600 °C in wet and dry Ar, respectively. This study indicated that perovskite electrolyte BCZYZn10 is a promising material for the next generation intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells (IT-SOFCs).

articleTitle: Catalytic chelation method for the removal of heavy metals (Pb, Ni and Cd) from Paphia textile
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Paphia textile is a shellfish which widely consumed by the society and it can be contaminated with heavy metals due to the increasing in domestic and industrial activities. This research was carried out to study the efficiency of catalytic chelation technique to remove heavy metals like lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd) and nickel (Ni) from Paphia textile. Three types of chelating agents, namely trisodium citrate, sodium acetate and disodium oxalate and three types of catalysts supported on Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> namely MgO, CaO and BaO were used. The treatment conditions were carried out using chelating agent at 400 mg/L, one-hour treatment time and treatment temperature of 32.50 ± 0.50°C. Metal concentrations were analyzed using Flame atomic absorption spectroscopy (FAAS). The initial concentrations of Pb, Ni and Cd in P. textile were 1.77±0.09 μg/g, 0.82±0.07 μg/g and 0.85±0.00 μg/g and removed to 84.69%, 78.60% and 41.96% respectively after chelation treatment. The trend of chelating agent followed the order of trisodium citrate, sodium acetate and disodium oxalate. Further treatment using catalyst revealed CaO/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> catalysts gave the highest percentage removal with 87.79% of Pb, 83.56% of Ni and 76.43% of Cd at an optimum calcination temperature of 1000°C. This study had successfully proven that catalytic chelation technique is able to enhance the removal of heavy metals compared to chelation technique from P. textile to achieve permissible limits set by Malaysian Food Regulation (Cd and Ni: 1.00 μg/g; Pb: 2.00 μg/g) and Commission Regulation of European Union (Cd and Ni: 1.00 μg/g; Pb: 1.50 μg/g).

articleTitle: Availability of timber waste and its current uses in Brunei Darussalam
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Brunei Darussalam's energy production is mostly dependent on fossil fuels which are a non-renewable energy source and are rapidly depleting thus the urgency to look for an alternative energy which is economical and able to sustain the great demand of energy for years, but not at the expense of the environment. This study looks into the availability of local timber waste that could potentially be utilised as biomass feedstock i.e. the quantification of average timber waste generated annually and its current utilisations. The investigation includes site visits to each sawmill to determine the log input, sawn-timber production, and utilisations of the timber wastes annually. On average sawmill generates a volume of timber waste that comprises of about 14.62% barks, 8.42% edgings and 25.89% sawdust. Since the production of sawmills are capped at 100,000 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, it is estimated that in a year, approximately 14,620 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of barks, 8,420 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of edgings and 25,890 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of sawdust are produced. The amount of waste generated each year fluctuates depending on the weather conditions, logs harvest allocations, capacity of sawmill and wood species. The findings from this research are beneficial in establishing the potential utilisation of timber waste as biomass feedstock.

articleTitle: GIS application in detecting forest and bush fire risk areas in Brunei Darussalam: Case analysis on Muara and Belait districts
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The land of Brunei Darussalam is approximately 75 percent under forest cover. These forests belong to six major types, each presenting numerous variants like mangrove forests, peat swamps forests located on waterlogged areas and fresh water swamps located along the river banks, health forests are located on white sands and mountain forests are located on higher altitude, the pristine forested peat land ecosystem has attracted the attention to the global communities. The findings show peat swamps forest covers 17% of the total land area comparing to freshwater swamp forest and mangrove forest which covers 2 percent and 3 percent of the total land area respectively. Over 30 percent of the peat land swamp forest are used for agriculture and 30 percent of peat land forest degraded to log. Moreover, peat swamp forests are prone to forest fire which is the new threat for virgin green forest and ecology of Brunei. The study area has focused on 2 districts in Brunei Darussalam (Brunei Muara and Belait district) with recurring fire calamities with the past 3 years period (2014–2016). The forest and bush fire shows the different new patches within the time frame in Brunei Muara district and Belait district. To perform spatial analysis and produce maps on risk areas of forest and bush fire in Brunei Darussalam through application of Remote Sensing (RS) and Geographical Information System (GIS) software towards detect and monitoring for protective management of forest.

articleTitle: Synthesis, structural and thermal properties of double perovskite NdSrMn2O6 as potential anode materials for solid oxide fuel cells
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This work reports the synthesis, structural and thermal characterisation of the double perovskite NdSrMn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> pointedly establishing their potential as anode materials for solid oxide fuel cells. The specimen was synthesized by solid state reaction method in air at 1400°C for 12 hours. Structural characterization was performed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). Rietveld analysis of the XRD data was evaluated by FullProf program and confirmed the single phase in orthorhombic symmetry (Pmmm space group). SEM images showed porous structures which should be suitable as anode materials for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs).

articleTitle: Impact of RF and leds on plants growth
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: The agriculture sector is one of the most important sectors supporting the Gross National Product of many countries throughout globe. Improving the agricultural productivity with minimal natural resources is the possible solution to mitigate the worldwide food shortage. This paper discusses a new useful agricultural method by using electromagnetic fields to improve the seed germination and crop yields. Also, this study explored the possible impacts of LEDs with different colours to enhance seed germination. These applications may also have had a positive effect on increasing crop production in the longer term. This research focuses in studying the impact of electromagnetic field, red and blue LEDs on cucumber and marigold plants and analysing the plants after the application of these electromagnetic field treatments. The EM field was produced using RF transmitter of 2.4 GHz with horn antenna to expose the experiment plants to the maximum in order to get the best possible outcome.

articleTitle: Demand-based photovoltaic orientation and power flow assessments of a 11 kV network
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic system is widely adopted for clean energy. Solar irradiance on PV panel is varied by the sun movement. In most installations, the orientation viz. azimuth and tilt angle of PV panel is optimised for maximum solar irradiance and energy production. The correlation between PV system production and load demand is not given due consideration, leading to poor correlation in most cases. In this paper, a sensitivity study on PV panel orientation is carried out. The aim is to evaluate the correlation between PV system energy production and measured feeder demand of a distribution network in Brunei, in terms of the Pearson correlation coefficient (r). Power flow assessments of the distribution network corresponding to the PV production profile of selected orientations are then performed. With PV arrays tilted at 20° and 30° and facing due West, the r are increased by 0.384 and 0.496, respectively, in comparison to the orientation optimised for energy production at 4° tilt, facing due South. The correlation improvement is associated with slight annual energy production reduction and increment in total line losses. Anyhow, reverse power flow is avoided in the network, thus diminishing the likelihood of voltage violation at the point of common coupling.

articleTitle: Determination of resonance wavelengths for photonic MUX DE-MUX using 50μm radius reference ring resonator
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: In this paper, it is determined and analysed that the resonance wavelengths for Photonic Multiplexer (MUX) and De-multiplexer (DE-MUX) using 50μιη radius reference ring resonator. To design optical MUX and DE-MUX, it is important to determine resonance wavelengths for various radius of the ring at suitable interval without overlapping of resonance wavelengths. The radius of the ring is varied from 50μm at interval of 20μm, 15μm, 10μm and 5μm, respectively and the analysed results are used to determine the number of channel that can be accommodated at various radius of ring with varies intervals. It is deduced that when the radius of the ring was varied from 50μm at 20μm, 15μm, 10μm and 5μm, the number of channels accommodated are three, four, five and ten, respectively. articleTitle: A comprehensive method to evaluate energy efficiency of industrial consumers
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: It is necessary to make an accurate assessment on energy efficiency of industrial consumers before implementing an energy-saving scheme. Several existing evaluation methods on energy efficiency have been criticized for their inaccurate indices, limited access to data and strong subjectivity. In this context, a new comprehensive evaluation method is presented on the basis of electric parameters of industrial consumers. In the proposed method, the evaluation indices are based on electric parameters, which can be accurately measured and recorded by smart meters. The well-established principal component analysis (PCA) is next used to eliminate the inessential indices, and then to attain the final evaluation system. Then, the weights of all indices are calculated using the entropy weight method and subsequently the fuzzy evaluation method is employed considering the fuzziness of evaluation results. Finally, an actual example is served for demonstrating the feasibility and features of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Power delay profile classification of quasi-deterministic channel
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Since the publication of Krizhevsky et. al. paper on image classification using convolutional neural networks, and the progress in so-called deep learning that followed, researchers are exploring applications in non-artificial intelligence areas. This work describes the application of a three-layer feedforward neural network for classifying wireless communication scenarios derived from a geometric stochastic channel model. Simulation results show the network's ability to classify four scenarios having distinct ensemble average power delay profiles with successful prediction of 90% on the test set. If the scenario conditions are modified so that the ensemble average power delay profiles are no longer distinct, the model accuracy on the test set drops to 54%. Thus, the viability of the classification depends on the information (features) that can be extracted from the data input to the neural network.

articleTitle: Energy saving potential in residential sector and its impact on power planning — A case study of the main interconnected system (MIS) of Oman
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a study done at SQU that assessed and evaluated the suitable, feasible and effective Demand Side Management (DSM) measures that can achieve substantial reduction in peak demand and electricity consumption in the residential villas/houses. The study, which is based on a survey of typical design of villas/houses and their energy consumption pattern, developed a simulation model using Design Builder, Energy Plus and MATLAB software. The simulation model is then used to investigate the energy saving potential in the residential sector by generating different scenarios of energy conservation measure. The results have shown a good energy saving which reaches up to 21.5% by using energy efficient designs for the houses and critical appliances such as air conditioning and lighting. The study then investigates the impact of energy conservation measures on generation capacity and energy savings using generation expansion planning software called WASP. The study also estimates environmental, transmission and distribution costs saving. The study estimates around 3.26 billion US dollars benefit for the coming 25 years.

articleTitle: Barriers and strategies for lean and green in construction projects in Australia
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Construction projects in many countries, including Australia need a radical change to effectively reduce wastes and enhance efficient productivity. Many benefits of lean and green paradigms would be comprehensively realised only if prevalent obstacles are thoroughly diagnosed and appropriate ways to overcome those obstacles are found. Based on a recent literature review, a set of barriers and strategies for lean and green in construction projects are compiled and reported in this paper. Also, the discussions include a summary of perceptions collated through semi-structured interviews conducted with 18 experienced design professionals in Australia. The thematic analysis reported in this paper revealed: (a) six major clusters of barriers including economic, procurement, technical, legislative, social and cultural, and organizational barriers; and (b) three expansive clusters of strategies for effective implementation of lean-green paradigm: education and training, legislation and contract controls, and economic and technical aspects.

articleTitle: LTE path-loss prediction models' comparative study for outdoor wireless communications
publicationTitle: 7th Brunei International Conference on Engineering and Technology 2018 (BICET 2018)
abstract: Propagation Pathloss models are key elements when planning communication networks where improper selection leads to high co-channel interference as well power and resources waste. This is an important element in the energy budget of each mobile cells. For this reason, it is necessary to estimate or measure path loss with such precision and accuracy as to provide effective and stable connection in the coverage area. The empirical models are used in the frequency range (1700–2100 MHz) which is necessary for the implementation of 4G LTE networks worldwide. In this study, the propagation models are studied for the frequencies used for 4G-LTE cells. The models are then compared with the experimentally collected data sets for different cells. This modelling process has been achieved through four main stages. Firstly, a rigorous drive test was conducted. Secondly, the measured path loss data has been handled using developed MATLAB scripts and compared to the predicted data of selected propagation models utilizing RMSE. Thirdly, the generalized equations of path loss models have been generated for each area and technology using the average RMSE value for each studied field and use of neural network for prediction.
